physicalNotes: Radius 0.46302158 Jupiter radii from Grouffal et al. 2026 (2026arXiv260623103G), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260623103G/abstract): 33,102.3 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0239752 Jupiter masses (Grouffal et al. 2026, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2026arXiv260623103G), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026arXiv260623103G/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Grouffal et al. 2026 (2026arXiv260623103G), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname GROUFFAL_ET_AL_2026): P 393 d
sources.shape: Grouffal et al. 2026 (2026arXiv260623103G), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname GROUFFAL_ET_AL_2026): a/R* derived by Kepler's third law from its period 393 d, stellar mass 1.22 and radius 1.3 solar units; Berardo et al. 2019 (2019AJ....157..185B), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname BERARDO_ET_AL__2019): inclination 89.91 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Grouffal et al. 2026 (2026arXiv260623103G), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname GROUFFAL_ET_AL_2026): transit mid-time 2457142.018 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 43200 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
